sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the appellants after referring to impugned award as well as evidence on record submits that Tribunal has not awarded sufficient amount of compensation.
In view of age and academic qualification of the deceased, Tribunal should have awarded appropriate compensation.
Therefore, appeal filed by the appellant be allowed and compensation awarded by the Tribunal be suitably enhanced.
4. Learned counsel for the respondents 1 and 2 have supported the findings recorded by the Tribunal and prays for dismissal of this appeal.
5. Learned counsel for the respondent No.3 submits that appropriate compensation amount has been awarded by the Tribunal.
Hence, no enhancement is required in the present case.

Therefore,
appeal filed by appellants be dismissed.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
6. So far as quantum of compensation is concerned, in the instant case, deceased was aged about 12 years.
As per para 25 of the impugned award, Tribunal has assessed annual income of the deceased as Rs.30000/- and 40% future prospects has been added and has applied multiplier of 20.
It has awarded Rs.40,000-/ as consortium and Rs.15,000/- for loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- for funeral expenses.

Tribunal has applied higher multiplier in the instant case and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is also on the higher side but as there are no cross objection/cross appeal, hence, no interference is required in the same.
Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.5,30,000/- .
In view of above facts and circumstances of the case, no enhancement is required in the instant case.
7. Accordingly, appeal filed by the appellant is dismissed.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Hashmi Raju Ahirwar vs Devraj on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117383675/
